limitations: Actions results apply only to this exact source SHA. Historical failures remain unchanged.
Producer executable/native-library inventories whose bytes are absent from the ZIP are supplier receipts, not independent verification of those binaries.
Hosted browser/media/network success does not establish physical GPU, real device, public NAT/HA, cross-day or release eligibility.
interpretation: All five original jobs completed successfully at source a1afd8b, including actual Chrome, Firefox and Microsoft Edge production Web-to-native hosted flows. Edge uses a Chromium engine and retains browser_product=edge.

Original Web UI, real local WebRTC/VP8/Opus, owned input recording and SCTP tempfile transfers, renewal and cleanup receipts passed. Capture is synthetic; no installed-platform or physical GPU acceptance is claimed.
The host terminal transport/cancellation diagnostic is preserved verbatim; final producer browser/native exit codes are zero and cleanup receipts are retained.

The browser progress_sha256 fields cover private raw JSONL. Python publish_receipts sanitizes and reserializes the public JSONL, so three private-raw digests cannot be independently verified from public bytes. All 58 public artifact files have independent actual-byte hashes and all six official ZIP digests match.
Release-site lock evidence includes before, after locked metadata and after build lock bytes plus a zero-byte diff; all four producer entries independently match.
The historical f24b79f Firefox 403/timeout evidence and 760f232 native-build failures remain unchanged. This later success does not change their conclusions.
